verdict.summary: Issue #213 remains blocked by seven specification defects affecting admission, deterministic classification, evidence production, secret handling, receipt provenance, and exact-version reproducibility.

blockingFindings.title: Disabled routes have no valid path into admission probing
blockingFindings.details: Routes begin disabled, and the contract requires disabled routes to be rejected before dispatch with the outcome matching their persistent reason. It also requires a successful first live proof to move a disabled route into probing, including recovery of Codex and Agy. No eligible-but-disabled state, runtime-owned admission exception, or pre-proof transition permits that dispatch. Define the exact transition that allows credential-gated admission while retaining pre-dispatch rejection for administratively disabled and decommissioned routes.

blockingFindings.title: Concurrent gate failures lack deterministic precedence
blockingFindings.details: Administrative state, proof expiry, credential state, quota state, billing eligibility, route availability, receipt validation, and secret-leak detection can overlap, but the contract does not define which outcome and transition takes precedence. This can change the required terminal classification for Kimi, Agy, and Codex. Specify a complete gate evaluation order, including which stages may inspect credential-owner metadata and which may perform network dispatch.

blockingFindings.title: No command deterministically produces required disabled-route evidence
blockingFindings.details: Acceptance requires records for Codex, Agy, and Kimi in their disabled terminal states, including a non-dispatched Kimi record. The live command processes only currently eligible configured routes, observation processes probing routes, and evidence only validates existing records. Define provider-agnostic command behavior that enumerates every required route and emits schema-valid pre-dispatch records for ineligible routes without invoking them.

blockingFindings.title: The exhaustive transition model still has unmapped values
blockingFindings.details: A route disabled by the rollback kill switch has reason repeated_malformed_timeout, but that value is absent from normalizedOutcome even though later rejection must match the persistent reason. The allowed transitionAction keep_terminal_state also has no event mapping or invariant. Define exactly one valid record representation for every reachable persistent state and subsequent evaluation.

blockingFindings.title: Secret-leak failures cannot satisfy the mandatory evidence schema
blockingFindings.details: The state machine requires secret_leak_detected records and disabling transitions, while every admission record unconditionally requires secretScan.status to be passed. A scan that detects a leak cannot truthfully pass, so the required failure cannot be represented as schema-valid evidence. Separate detection records from sanitized publication validation or define an explicit detected/failed scan state and fail-closed publication rules.

blockingFindings.title: Immutable execution-receipt storage and reference provenance are undefined
blockingFindings.details: Issue #275 creates its receipt as a new file in the caller worktree, while #213 stores admission evidence in Andromeda-data and requires validators to reject references outside that evidence repository. The specification does not define the authoritative receipt repository, immutable commit identity, or byte-preserving transfer and reference procedure. Define those details without forking or reinterpreting the #275 schema.

blockingFindings.title: Admission evidence cannot prove the reviewed issue version
blockingFindings.details: Admission records and publication markers identify the implementation target revision but omit the canonical digest of the complete issue version. Publication-time comparison therefore depends on transient run context and cannot later associate evidence with the reviewed specification or deterministically invalidate it after an edit. Add the exact issue-version identity to records and markers and require evidence validation against the complete current issue version.

nonBlockingNotes: Issues #253, #275, #291, and #293 remain explicit dependencies or recovery owners; their open state is sequencing evidence, not an additional specification defect.
No additional owner-only policy choice is required if the specified terminal provider states are retained.
